_readme: THE DEMO SET: plans a visitor may open on any box, ours and only ours.
THE DEMO TAB IS THIS FILE. /api/demo-plans answers from here alone, so
the tab shows exactly these plans, one card each, on a box holding zero
jobs for them or sixty-three. It is NOT built from job rows any more:
that showed the box's history (15 jobs for Oncor, 14 for Belle Farms
Structural) and every one of them carried a detection computed weeks
ago, which is a pre-warmed cache presented as a live run.
AND THEY OPEN FRESH. POST /api/demo/{name}/open sweeps everything
derived from the PDF before handing it over, so a visitor always meets
an UNDETECTED document and presses Detect themselves. One job per plan
is reused for that, so opening a demo three times does not grow the
registry by three rows - see server.py _demo_job.
One source of truth, read by four things:
server.py       /api/demo-plans renders the cards from this file;
/api/demo/{name}/open opens one fresh; and a job row
is still flagged demo:true when its display name is a
key below AND the row is owner-less (the existing
shared/owner visibility rule - a client upload that
happens to carry the same filename is NEVER a demo),
which is what keeps demo jobs off Your projects.
webui/app.js    draws the Demo tab from /api/demo-plans; a plan whose
PDF is not on this box still gets a card, saying so.
seed-demo.sh    uploads these onto a hosted box, and refuses to run if
it does not seed every name here. Any pre-detection it
does is swept by the first demo open, by design.
provision_demo.py  keeps owner=None on exactly these when it hands
every other document on the box to staff.
The key is the DISPLAY name, which is the filename with our own
upload_<hash>_ prefix stripped (server.py _display_name). That is what
makes one list work for a laptop that opened the file by path and for a
hosted box that received it through /api/upload.
PROVENANCE RULE, not negotiable: every file here is ours - the
TakeoffPro AI corpus (Plans, Plans 2) or the Oncor sheet beside it.
Nothing from Ryno Construction and nothing from client_meet may ever
appear in this file: those are named clients' drawings, and stice /
Liberty Park is a live bid. tests/test_projects_api.py enforces this.
`page` is the sheet a visitor should land on (engine page index, 0-based
- printed sheet number is page+1 on these sets).
`shows` is printed on the card. EVERY ONE OF THESE LINES WAS WRITTEN
FROM A LIVE RUN ON THAT SHEET, 2026-08-31, not from what a sheet of its
type usually carries - see out/verify/2026-08-31/projects-landing/. If
you add a plan, open it and detect it first, and describe what actually
came out. A card that promises a capability the sheet does not exercise
is the one thing a demo set must never do.
DROPPED after testing, and why:
window_takeoff_benchmark_plan.pdf - it opens and detects fine (44
chains, 6 styles, scale read from its caption), but its own title
block reads 'AUTOMATION TAKEOFF BENCHMARK PLAN - WINDOW TEST BED /
PROJECT: MOCK-01'. It is our synthetic fixture, not a drawing, and a
visitor who opens it sees us demonstrating on a rectangle we drew
ourselves. It stays in the corpus as a test bed; it is not a demo.
This leaves symbol COUNTING undemonstrated - the only counting sheets
in the corpus (Marked Up Window Plans, Window - Storefront - Door
schedules) are under client_meet/Bill and are excluded by the rule
above. That gap is real and is not papered over here.

Oncor Cloudcrest Substation Civils - 202.shows: Substation civils drawn with no CAD layer names at all — 314 runs sorted into 49 styles by line pattern alone.

C4.0-SITE-GRADING-PLAN-Rev.1.pdf.shows: The densest sheet we score: 1,429 runs in 113 styles, every one carrying the drafter's own layer name.

Belle Farms Structural Plans.pdf.shows: A building sheet, not a civil one — and the only one here whose scale is confirmed twice: printed and drawn agree.

Belle Farms Upper Parcel ROAD GRADING 1.shows: Heavy topography: 685 contour runs, 254k ft of line. It prints three scales, and the app refuses to pick one for you.

C6.0-WATER-MAIN-PLAN-AND-PROFILE-Rev.1.p.shows: Wet utilities, plan and profile on one page — water, gas and electric runs above, the profile band below.

C8.0-STORM-LAYOUT-Rev.1.pdf.shows: A storm drain network: O-PIPE runs between structures. Its scale came from OCR, and the app says not to trust that.

GCHC North Stairs Plan 1 Grading.pdf.shows: The cleanest read in the set — 52 of its 53 styles arrive already named by the drafter, leaving one thing to check.
